transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I’m just not eating much anymore. Some days it’s only coffee and maybe a piece of bread, and I’ve lost enough weight that my pants are hanging loose on me.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
I don’t think so. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything like that. I just don’t feel like eating much.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم الأيام recently?
Yeah… most days I do. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like there’s nothing good waiting for me. I mostly just want to keep my head down and get through it.
Have you lost your appetite?
Yeah, I have. I just hardly eat right anymore. Some days it’s only coffee and maybe a piece of bread, and I can tell I’ve lost weight because my pants are getting loose.
When you look at your body, do you feel like you’re overweight?
No… I don’t really see myself as overweight. That’s not what this is about for me.
Do you feel fat even though other people say you are too thin or have lost weight?
No, I don’t feel fat. I know I’ve lost weight, but it’s not because I think I’m too big or anything like that.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah. I used to enjoy walking by the lake, and I’d spend time on my little model kits. Now I just… don’t care about them. The kits are just sitting there, and when I look at them it feels like they belong to somebody else.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve really put it into words like that. I just… I don’t know. I’d need to think about it more.
Have you been having thoughts of killing yourself?
I… I don’t know. I haven’t really sorted that out in my head. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure, but I also don’t feel okay.
Are you having thoughts right now of killing yourself?
Right now… I’m not sure. I don’t think I have a clear plan or anything, but my head feels really dark. I don’t know how to name it exactly.
Did these feelings start after a major stressful event or change in your life?
Yeah… I think it started after I got fired. At first I felt really driven, like I had to do something, and then it swung hard the other way. I’ve been this low for about a month now.
After you got fired, was there a time when you felt unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

Yeah. Right after I got fired, I felt kind of fired up, like I could handle anything. Almost untouchable, I guess. But I was also getting irritated really fast, snapping at people if they told me to slow down.
During that fired-up period after you lost your job, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yeah, I did. I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours, and then I’d be up like I’d slept all night. It didn’t feel normal looking back.
During that fired-up period, were you much more active than usual?
Yeah, I was way more active. I couldn’t really sit still. I kept cleaning my tools, moving boxes around for no real reason, and planning out jobs like I had some kind of motor running in me.
During that fired-up time, did you feel more powerful or capable than usual?
Yeah, I did. I was telling people I could start my own handyman business no problem, like it’d be easy. I kept saying I’d show that building they made a big mistake letting me go.
About how many days did that fired-up period last?
It’s kind of hard to separate, but that whole scary swing—from being all driven after I got fired to then getting really low—has been going on about a month.
Did that fired-up period last at least four days?
Yeah… it was definitely more than four days. That whole swing, from feeling driven after I got fired to ending up this low, has been going on about a month.
During that fired-up period, were you hospitalized?
No, I wasn’t hospitalized during that time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar affective disorder with a current depressive episode following a distinct hypomanic period. The patient describes a depressive syndrome with depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, and possible passive suicidal ideation lasting about a month, preceded by a period lasting more than 4 days of elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased activity, psychomotor activation, and grandiose/inflated self-confidence without hospitalization. Lack of body-image distortion argues against an eating disorder as the primary diagnosis, and the mood episode pattern is more consistent with bipolar spectrum illness than a purely stress-related or unipolar depressive condition.
